learningObjective: Diagnose dynamic-shape performance regressions in compiled workloads from a mix of graph-break/recompile logs and per-shape latency data.
stem: A torch.compile-wrapped inference service handles requests of varying seq_len. In production, latency has become erratic. The following profiler output is captured. Which conclusions are supported? (Select all that apply.)
profileData:
Per-request torch.compile trace (500 requests, various seq_len):
  Seq_len distribution: 128, 256, 384, 512, 640, 768, 896, 1024 (roughly uniform)
  torch._dynamo.utils.count_calls_to_compile: 8 recompiles (one per unique seq_len)
  torch._dynamo.config.cache_size_limit: default (8)
  Median latency:  4.2 ms  (steady state after warmup)
  p95 latency:     42.6 ms
  p99 latency:     58.1 ms
  First-time-seen seq_len latencies:  350 - 900 ms
  Recompile reason in logs: "tensor size mismatch, previous s0 = 128, new s0 = 256" (× 7)

options.text: Enabling dynamic shapes (e.g., `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` or `torch._dynamo.mark_dynamic`) would allow one compiled graph to cover multiple seq_lens, converting the recompile spikes into a single warmup cost and stabilizing p95/p99.

The `cache_size_limit` of 8 is currently being fully consumed and the FX cache is thrashing on the present 8-shape workload; each of the 8 shapes is being evicted and recompiled every invocation, which is why recompilation is being observed.

The recompile latencies (~350–900 ms) are counted inside the per-request latency measurement, so the p95/p99 are dominated by compile-time cost, not actual GPU execution. Removing the compile cost by pre-warming all seq_lens or enabling dynamic shapes would fix the tail.

The 8 recompiles correspond to shape-specialized graphs — one per unique seq_len — because dynamic shape was not enabled (or a guard forced specialization); the p99 spikes correspond to first-time-seen shapes paying the JIT cost.

explanation: Options A, C, D are correct; option B is incorrect. A (Correct): dynamic-shape compile addresses the root cause. B (Wrong): with exactly 8 distinct shapes and cache_size_limit=8, the cache is at capacity but NOT evicting — each shape's compiled artifact is still resident, so no thrashing/eviction is occurring. Recompilation being observed must therefore come from a different cause (guard failures on non-shape state, dynamic=True disabled, or a Python-level cache miss unrelated to size_limit). The "currently thrashing" claim is factually wrong given the present state. C (Correct): JIT cost is inside the request latency for first-time-seen shapes. D (Correct): matches the guard-based recompile behavior. General context: If shape diversity were higher, C's concern would be legitimate, but the specific data given here does not evidence eviction — the observed pattern is one-time recompile cost, not thrashing.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: with exactly 8 distinct shapes and cache_size_limit=8, the cache is at capacity but NOT evicting — each shape's compiled artifact is still resident, so no thrashing/eviction is occurring. Recompilation being observed must therefore come from a different cause (guard failures on non-shape state, dynamic=True disabled, or a Python-level cache miss unrelated to size_limit). The "currently thrashing" claim is factually wrong given the present state.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: JIT cost is inside the request latency for first-time-seen shapes.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: matches the guard-based recompile behavior.

assumptions: Static-shape torch.compile mode (no explicit dynamic=True or mark_dynamic).
nonImplications: Does not imply dynamic=True has no drawbacks; guards and shape-generic kernels can be slower per iteration.
Does not imply larger cache_size_limit is always the right fix; it hides but does not eliminate compile cost.

distractorRationales.B: Concern would apply to a different data regime; not supported by these numbers.

performanceClaim.scope: torch.compile inference with static-shape guards under varying seq_len
